item.title: The Alpha Clustering Model of the EMC Effect
item.description: arXiv:2611.13234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For more than forty years, the EMC effect, the observation that nuclear structure functions in deep-inelastic scattering appear to be modified relative to the free-nucleon expectation, has resisted a consensus microscopic explanation. In this letter, we argue that the strength and $A$ dependence of the EMC effect may be governed by the phenomena of $\alpha$ clustering in nuclei and responsible for a majority of the partonic modification associated with the EMC Effect. We motivate the alpha clustering model of the EMC effect (ACME), and with a data driven approach, we demonstrate how such a model can reproduce the existing deep inelastic scattering data on nuclei. We make predictions for other nuclei such as $^{16}$O, $^{20}$Ne, and $^{48}$Ca and explore its consequences for a spin-dependent EMC effect and global analysis of nuclear parton distributions.
item.dc:creator: Whitney Armstrong

item.title: Coherent control of quadrupolar order in solid spin-1 systems:\ majorization bounds, orientation-indexed adiabatic inversion, and order lifetime
item.description: arXiv:2611.13408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tensor polarization $\Pzz=1-3p_0$ of spin-1 nuclei in dynamically polarized solid targets is limited, under a single spin temperature, to $\Pzz^{\rm eq}=2-\sqrt{4-3P^2}$ ($\Pzz\simeq0.20$ at vector polarization $P=0.5$). Radio-frequency (rf) semi-saturation of one quadrupolar Pake-doublet branch, with and without slow sample rotation, has reached $\Pzz\simeq0.36$. Using the first-order quadrupole Hamiltonian, spin temperatures of the Zeeman and alignment (quadrupolar-order) reservoirs, and single-transition operators, we analyze these manipulations. Five results follow. (i) Under unital operations (rf pulses, rotation, saturation), $1-3\lambda_{\max}\le\Pzz\le1-3\lambda_{\min}$, where $\lambda_{\min,\max}$ are the smallest and largest initial populations. Saturation achieves at most half the available transfer; selective $\pi$ inversion reaches either bound ($\Pzz=-0.85,+0.65$ at $P=0.5$). (ii) In a powder, the two single-quantum transitions overlap except in the pedestal region. Adiabatic frequency sweeps confined there invert one transition per bond. Inverting each bond exactly once requires packing antipodal caps on the orientation sphere. The optimal single-axis arrangement has four stops at the magic angle $54.74\degree$ (cube body diagonals; 73\% coverage); six icosahedral axes give the global optimum (90\%). (iii) Rotation-induced Landau--Zener crossings of deuteron pairs are adiabatic at current rates and scramble the inversion pattern; transits must be fast for the strongest, geminal CD$_2$, pairs. (iv) A parity theorem determines the inverted bonds solely from the endpoints of continuous adiabatic passage: rf during rotation yields at most two caps, and a full turn none. (v) The enhanced state decays by dipolar flip-flops, with $T_{1Q}\le T_{1Z}/3$ and a duty-cycle break-even of $\simeq35$~min. Magic-angle spinning cannot replace this scheme.
item.dc:creator: D. Keller, M. F. Hossain

item.title: Nuclear medium and final state interaction effects in $\eta$ production induced by $\nu_\mu(\bar\nu_\mu)$ at SBN and DUNE energies
item.description: arXiv:2611.13602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate nuclear-medium modification and final-state interaction in charged- and neutral-current $\nu_\mu(\bar{\nu}_\mu)$-induced $\eta$-meson production on $^{12}\mathrm{C}$ and $^{40}\mathrm{Ar}$. The nuclear medium is described within a local density approximation, incorporating in-medium modifications of the $N^*(1535)$ resonance, which is known to play the dominant role in $\eta$ production through its $N \eta$ decay channel. The subsequent propagation and absorption of the $\eta$ meson in the nucleus are simulated using a Monte Carlo approach. We find that nuclear-medium modifications and final state interaction lead to substantial suppression of the production cross section, highlighting the importance of nuclear effects in interpreting $\eta$ production data. Our results provide valuable theoretical input for the analysis of $\eta$-production at the ongoing SBND and MicroBooNE experiments and the forthcoming DUNE experiment.
item.dc:creator: A. Fatima, S. K. Noor Alam, M. Sajjad Athar, S. K. Singh

item.title: Density dependence of effective Lambda-nucleon interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.13721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Orbital-dependent $\Lambda$ binding energies in hypernuclei such as $^{208}_{\Lambda}$Pb, $^{40}_{\Lambda}$K, and $^{48}_{\Lambda}$K are important objectives of planned experiments at J-PARC and JLab and provide information on the density-dependent features of effective $\Lambda N$ interactions. To investigate this relation we introduce the environmental density $\bar{\rho}_\text{env}$, defined as the overlap integral of the \Lambda and nuclear core densities, as quantitative measure of the nuclear environment experienced by the $\Lambda$ in each orbital. Calculations are performed within the deformed Skyrme-Hartree-Fock framework, comparing several phenomenological and microscopic $\Lambda N$ interactions. We find an approximately linear relation between the orbital-dependent binding energies and $\bar{\rho}_\text{env}$, offering a quantitative means to test and refine effective $\Lambda N$ interactions using future orbital-dependent binding-energy data.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Zeng, Xian-Rong Zhou, Yu-Gang Ma, H. -J. Schulze

item.title: Triangular and fourth-order flow of D mesons in Pb-Pb collisions with event-by-event fluctuations
item.description: arXiv:2611.13891v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Charm quarks are valuable probes of the transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma (QGP), yet the role of event-by-event medium fluctuations in shaping their observables remains to be quantified. We study this problem in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02$~TeV by coupling the iEBE-VISHNU event-by-event viscous hydrodynamic framework to a Langevin transport model with instantaneous coalescence hadronization. We find that fluctuations have little effect on the azimuthally averaged $D$ meson nuclear modification factor $R_{AA}$, which remains close to the smooth-background baseline with only modest momentum-dependent deviations. In contrast, the anisotropic flow coefficients $v_n$ are increasingly sensitive to fluctuations with rising harmonic order $n$. In particular, the triangular flow $v_3$, which vanishes in the smooth background, is entirely generated by initial-state fluctuations, and our results reproduce the main features of the available CMS measurements. We further present predictions for the $D$ meson $v_4$, which provide a quantitative benchmark for future measurements of higher-order heavy-flavor flow and help elucidate the interplay between event-by-event QGP fluctuations and charm quark dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Yiyun Tang, Jiamin Liu, Yunpeng Liu, Baoyi Chen

item.title: M-SHIVA 1.0: A Relativistic Resistive MHD Code for Heavy-Ion Collisions, with Applications to Momentum Anisotropy and Joule Heating in QGP
item.description: arXiv:2611.13899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present M-SHIVA 1.0 (Magneto-resistive Solver for Heavy Ions with finite-Volume Algorithms), a (2+1)-dimensional relativistic resistive magnetohydrodynamics code for heavy-ion collisions in Cartesian and boost-invariant Milne coordinates. The present implementation treats inviscid dynamics and employs an implicit-explicit (IMEX) Runge-Kutta scheme for the stiff conductivity-dependent terms, together with complementary primitive-variable recovery procedures and generalized Lagrange multiplier (GLM) divergence cleaning. The code reproduces standard shock-tube, cylindrical-blast-wave and relativistic-rotor benchmarks. We use the framework to investigate the momentum anisotropy and electromagnetic energy transfer in an expanding quark-gluon plasma (QGP). In a controlled elliptic-fireball setup, the electromagnetic field modifies the total momentum anisotropy mainly through its direct contribution to the transverse stress tensor, while the matter anisotropy is only weakly affected. We further separate the electromagnetic work into mechanical Lorentz-force work and irreversible Joule heating. Applications to Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 62.4$ and $200$ GeV and Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 2.76$ TeV employ optical-Glauber matter profiles, spectator-generated electromagnetic fields, and a temperature-dependent electrical conductivity motivated by lattice-QCD results. The ratio of Joule heating to expansion cooling is approximately $10^{-14}$-$10^{-11}$ for Pb+Pb collisions at $2.76$ TeV, $10^{-8}$-$10^{-5}$ for Au+Au collisions at $200$ GeV and $10^{-7}$-$10^{-4}$ at $62.4$ GeV, with no appreciable conductivity dependence of the matter or total momentum anisotropy. Resistive heating thus grows by orders of magnitude with decreasing collision energy but remains negligible compared with longitudinal expansion cooling for all systems considered.
item.dc:creator: Krishanu Sengupta, Victor Roy

item.title: Formation of superheavy elements 119 and 120 in the $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Bk and $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Cf reactions: dinuclear system dynamics, survival probability, and decay chains of the evaporation residues
item.description: arXiv:2611.13953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Bk and $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Cf reactions leading to the compound nuclei $^{299}$119 and $^{299}$120 are studied in the framework of the dinuclear system (DNS) model. The capture cross section has been calculated by solving the dynamical equations of motion for all orientation angles of the deformed target nucleus and for the zero-point vibrations of the projectile. The charge distribution of the DNS fragments has been obtained from the transport master equation with transition rates obeying detailed balance, and the compound nucleus formation probability has been calculated as the branching ratio of the level densities over the intrinsic fusion, quasifission, and symmetry barriers. The survival probability has been calculated in the Hauser-Feshbach formalism for every excitation energy and angular momentum of the compound nucleus, with the fission barriers of the macroscopic-microscopic model with triaxial saddle points. The normalization of the saddle-point level density has been fixed by the measured evaporation residue (ER) cross sections of the $^{48}$Ca+$^{244}$Pu reaction. The largest ER cross sections are obtained in the 3n channel, 18 fb at $E^*_\mathrm{CN}=32$ MeV for $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Cf and 27 fb at 33 MeV for $^{50}$Ti+$^{249}$Bk. At the energy of the GSI experiments, the calculated sums of the 3n and 4n cross sections, 4 and 6 fb, respectively, are well below the upper limits of 200 and 65 fb obtained there. With the normalization refitted, the alternative mass tables and fission barriers considered here give the maximum 3n cross sections smaller by up to a factor of 25. The $\alpha$-decay chains of the residues have been predicted; the isotopes of element 120 are expected to have half-lives of 1-12 $\mu$s and those of element 119 of 16-230 $\mu$s.
item.dc:creator: Bakhodir Kayumov

item.title: Neutron stars nearly close the window for muon-induced baryon-number violation
item.description: arXiv:2611.13954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Baryon-number violation that needs a muon in the initial state can evade proton-decay searches and be observed in muon capture at Mu2e and COMET. Neutron stars contain muons, so the same interaction converts their protons into dark baryons, but the rate of this conversion in dense matter and its consequences have not been computed. In this paper we compute the conversion rate, the heat it deposits, and the evolution of a star under fast conversion. The coldest known neutron stars exclude conversion rates far below laboratory reach for every dark-fermion mass that capture in aluminium can produce, and faster conversion burns stars down or, unless conserved dark baryons repel each other strongly enough, collapses them. The repulsion they need follows a scaling law in the baryonic mass headroom of the nucleonic equation of state, which applies to any process that puts dark baryons in equilibrium with neutrons.
item.dc:creator: Bharat Kumar

item.title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.14331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perturbative QCD, supplemented only by thermodynamic consistency, causality, and mechanical stability, constrains the equation of state of dense matter far below the densities at which the perturbative expansion itself converges. Until now, however, such constraints have been established only for cold, catalyzed matter. We show that this model-independent bound generalizes to finite temperature along adiabats labelled by the entropy per baryon $\hat{s}$, with the specific enthalpy $h=(\varepsilon+p)/n_{\mathrm{B}}$ assuming the role played by the baryon chemical potential at $T=0$. We find that increasing the temperature shrinks the allowed region monotonically in a form that is universal across structurally distinct mean-field families. For DD2, the density at which the equation of state becomes inconsistent with perturbative QCD decreases from $1.0$ to $0.74\,\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$ as $\hat{s}$ increases from $0$ to $5$, falling below the central density of the heaviest cold star. By $\hat{s}=4$, seven of eleven relativistic mean-field models are excluded at $6\,n_{\mathrm{sat}}$; approximately half of the equations of state drawn from two Bayesian posteriors are excluded by $\hat{s}\simeq3.4$--$4.4$. When mapped onto the QCD phase diagram, the bound becomes active at temperatures of $100$--$150$ MeV, precisely the regime transiently realized in neutron-star mergers and proto-neutron stars.
item.dc:creator: Tyler Gorda, Aleksi Kurkela, Tuhin Malik

item.title: Structure of correlations for the single-$j$ model using quantum information theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.14460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We say that a system undergoes a quantum phase transition when the mean-field ground state of a given Hamiltonian spontaneously breaks its symmetries depending on the Hamiltonian parameters. It is a widely accepted view that this phenomenon enables the mean-field state to absorb the maximum amount of correlations without losing its mean-field structure. However, it is still uncertain how those correlations are incorporated within the mean-field state and how the correlation structure changes when we get closer to the exact ground state by restoring the symmetries. In this work, we answer these questions by studying the single-$j$ model, which is a realistic fermionic nuclear model with abelian and non-abelian broken symmetries. We find that both types of symmetries have very different effects for the correlations within the mean-field state. This makes unclear the concept of the symmetry breaking process as a mechanism to absorb the maximum amount of correlations. Moreover, the symmetry restoration redistributes existing `fake' correlations between paired orbitals to more complex subsystems.
item.dc:creator: Javier Faba, Vicente Mart\'in, Luis Robledo

item.title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
item.description: arXiv:2611.09839v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants. This new definition is a parallel to the Gibbs entropy formulation, but it can also be used in out-of-equilibrium regimes. Some important properties of this entropy are discussed. In addition we derive some information theory quantities such as relative entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and R\'enyi entropy. We then compare the results with Wehrl entropy for the 1D harmonic oscillator, for pure and mixed states. We conclude the the work discussing potential applications of this new formalism, ranging from quantum correlations beyond entanglement to thermalization in closed quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Rabelo-Soares, Yevgeniy Kovchegov, Giorgio Torrieri

item.title: Nuclear geometry under external magnetic field in the Skyrme-Maxwell model
item.description: arXiv:2611.13152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We find static solutions of the U(1) gauged Skyrme-Maxwell model in a constant external magnetic field, for baryon numbers $B \leq 6$. The field acts as an isospin-breaking source, stretching the skyrmion along its direction, while its size grows and then shrinks as the induction increases. We obtain the energy minimizers with a GPU implementation of the arrested Newton flow (ANF) algorithm. Gauged skyrmions have less energy and are more strongly bound than their ungauged counterpart. At weak magnetic field, the solutions are small deformations of the ungauged skyrmions, including regions of negative baryon density in sectors $B = 3, 5, 6$. For intermediate field, novel geometries appear, notably a $(B-1)$-toroidal chain. High field values lead to axially symmetric toroidal structures for all $B$.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Adam, Andr\'es R. Anad\'on, Carlos Naya, Thomas Winyard

item.title: Thermal $CP$ dynamics in a four-fermion model: mean-field and functional renormalization group analyses
item.description: arXiv:2611.13405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate a one-flavor four-fermion model with scalar, pseudoscalar, and mixed scalar-pseudoscalar interactions at finite temperature and vanishing chemical potential. Our analysis combines the mean-field approximation, which determines the equilibrium condensates, with the functional renormalization group (FRG), which describes the scale dependence of the interactions and the fermion mass phase. Within the mean-field approach, we find that, in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking sources, the dominant interaction determines the direction of condensation. In particular, a pseudoscalar condensate spontaneously breaks the ordinary $P/CP$ symmetry and disappears through a continuous thermal phase transition. For regular high-temperature FRG trajectories, the dimensionless mixed coupling tends to zero in the infrared, while its dimensionful counterpart remains finite. Increasing temperature also suppresses the scale evolution of the fermion mass phase. Together, these results clarify the distinct roles of thermal fluctuations in suppressing spontaneous symmetry breaking and fermionic instabilities, without necessarily eliminating explicit symmetry breaking effects.
item.dc:creator: Arthur F. Vieira, Rudnei O. Ramos

item.title: Pseudoscalar meson masses in magnetic fields at zero temperature from lattice QCD
item.description: arXiv:2611.14080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study neutral and charged pseudoscalar meson masses in background magnetic fields in $(2+1)$-flavor QCD at zero temperature and physical quark masses. Using the highly improved staggered quark action at four lattice spacings, we obtain continuum-extrapolated masses from connected correlators for pions, kaons, and the fictitious $s\bar s$ pseudoscalar $\eta^0_{s\bar s}$. Neutral pseudoscalar masses decrease with increasing magnetic field, with the largest relative reduction for the neutral pion. In contrast, charged pion and kaon masses initially rise but tend to level off or decrease at stronger fields, departing from the point-particle lowest-Landau-level expectation. To investigate the origin of this field dependence, we compare neutral and charged pion masses at finite lattice spacings with the field included only in valence propagators or only in the sea-quark determinant. Valence-only masses approximately reproduce the full results, while sea-only masses remain close to their corresponding zero-field values.
item.dc:creator: Heng-Tong Ding, Dan Zhang

item.title: Nucleon sigma terms in lattice QCD at physical pion mass and in the continuum
item.description: arXiv:2611.14103v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the light, strange and charm $\sigma$-terms of the nucleon in lattice QCD using four $N_f=2+1+1$ twisted-mass gauge ensembles simulated at physical pion masses and with approximately the same spatial volumes. The four lattice spacings ranging from $0.080$ fm to $0.049$ fm, with an action that has O(a) improvement, enable extrapolating the results to the continuum limit. Both valence and sea quark contributions are analysed accounting for excited-state contamination from low-lying multihadron states. We perform global fits to all ensembles, that yield $\sigma_{\pi N}=53.0(7.4)(1.6)$ MeV, $\sigma_s=58.2(17.0)(2.1)$ MeV and $\sigma_c=112(28)(25)$ MeV, with statistical and systematic uncertainties, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Constantia Alexandrou, Christos Iona, Giannis Koutsou, Yan Li, Srijit Paul, Ferenc Pittler

item.title: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
item.description: arXiv:2611.14243v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. Using analytical Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi exterior solutions, we match stellar perturbations to an effective field theory and extract the poles and residues of the relativistic tidal response. Over the inspiral band, this response is accurately approximated by a sum of harmonic oscillators, as in Newtonian theory, each specified by a frequency $\omega_\alpha$ and a mode-specific tidal deformability $\lambda_\alpha$, or equivalently a tidal overlap $I_\alpha$. We couple these oscillators to relativistic effective-one-body dynamics, including gravitational redshift and frame dragging, to follow mode excitation and gravitational-wave emission. A decomposition into driven and free oscillations gives analytical mode amplitudes accurate to a few percent during inspiral. We also reconstruct the time-dependent crustal strain. In a representative $1.20+1.50\,M_\odot$ hadronic--hybrid binary, gravity, interface and shear modes produce a gravitational-wave phase shift of $\lesssim10^{-2}\,{\rm rad}$. Despite this small phase shift, gravity-mode excitation can overstrain the crust near its base, while the lowest shear mode produces widespread overstrain.
item.dc:creator: Yong Gao, Jan Steinhoff

item.title: Renormalization-group flow of nucleon--$\Delta$ contact interactions with an explicit $\Delta$: decoupling and the scale dependence of large-$N_c$ relations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the leading-order (LO) contact interactions among nucleons and $\Delta$ isobars under a Wilsonian renormalization-group flow with a sharp momentum cutoff, keeping the $\Delta$ as an explicit coupled channel, and determine which large-$N_c$ relations among the couplings are invariant under the flow. The two-channel flow with the $\Delta\Delta$ threshold inside the cutoff range is solved exactly, and the closed channels decouple with relative corrections of order $\Lambda^2/\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}^2$, where $\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}=\sqrt{2M_\Delta(M_\Delta-M_N)}$ is the closed-channel momentum. Applying the $1/N_c$ expansion of the Hartree Hamiltonian to the $N$--$\Delta$ system, we find that a generalized time reversal removes all corrections of relative order $1/N_c$, that the LO fixes eleven of the 18 S-wave couplings in terms of seven, and that the exact-SU(4) two-parameter form used in the literature differs from the LO by an operator of relative order $1/N_c^2$ with matrix elements of order one in the $\Delta$ channels. The eight spin--isospin flip relations are exact invariants of the flow, also when the central part of one-pion exchange is iterated in the S waves. The eigenchannel relations of the $NN$--$\Delta\Delta$ sectors hold only at the scale at which they are imposed. Their running is controlled by $\kappa_{\Delta\Delta}$, which is of order $N_c^0$, and by a parameter that the $NN$ data do not fix, so that the $1/N_c$ expansion does not remove it. Large-$N_c$ relations between open and closed channels therefore constrain the potential at one scale. The flip relation between the $(S,I)=(3,0)$ and $(0,3)$ channels of $\Delta\Delta$ scattering predicts equal scattering lengths at LO, which lattice QCD at heavy pion masses can test.
item.dc:creator: Dominador F. Vaso, Jr., Daris Samart, Jingle B. Magallanes

item.title: Spurious Isospin Breaking in the In-medium Similarity Renormalization Group
item.description: arXiv:2412.10693v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The in-medium similarity renormalization group is a promising ab initio approach for computing the isospin-related theoretical correction $\delta_C$ to superallowed beta decay rates, relevant for tests of CKM unitarity. An essential requirement of such corrections is a properly quantified theoretical uncertainty. While isospin symmetry is explicitly broken by internucleon forces, approximations made in the solving the many-body problem can also spuriously break the symmetry, obscuring the desired signal. In this work, we use a toy model to identify the primary sources of spurious isospin symmetry breaking introduced by the IMSRG many-body framework, and provide mitigation strategies for application in large-scale calculations.
item.dc:creator: A. Farren, S. R. Stroberg

item.title: Weinberg Angle, Neutron Abundance in BBN, and Lifetime
item.description: arXiv:2603.02652v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present state of the art kinetic theory determination of the neutron abundance available for the Big-Bang nucleosynthesis (BBN). Our work is motivated by the study of the neutron lifespan measured in the laboratory and the unknown strength of weak interactions coupling constant $G_\mathrm{F}$ at finite temperature in the primordial Universe. We draw attention to the relevant dependence of $G_\mathrm{F}$ on the symmetry breaking Weinberg angle $s^2_\mathrm{W}$, a free parameter in the standard model of particle physics. We establish how the value of $s^2_\mathrm{W}$ by way of $G_\mathrm{F}$ modification influences neutron abundance available for BBN and neutron lifetime.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Tao Yang, Johann Rafelski

item.title: Are neutrinos Majorana? Fixed-target and high-energy astrophysical searches decide
item.description:
arXiv:2606.17132v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The original version of this paper proposed a new approach to determining whether neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana fermions, a fundamental open question in particle physics. Conventional searches rely on neutrinoless double beta decay, but this electron-only channel suffers from blind spots. We propose a new, complementary probe to overcome this limitation. A heavy neutral lepton (HNL) triggers a high-energy shift in how the active neutrino flavors ($
u_e$, $
u_\mu$, $
u_	au$) mix---but only if the neutrinos are Majorana. For GeV-scale HNLs, the upcoming beam-dump experiment SHiP can discover the HNL and measure how it mixes with the active flavors. However, the proposed signature of the Majorana nature of neutrinos does not exist. The reasons are explained here. The analysis has been superseded by Ref.~\cite{Barenboim:2026udr}. The original version is retained as v1 for the record.
item.dc:creator: Gabriela Barenboim, Mauricio Bustamante, Qinrui Liu

item.title: Production Effects and Final-state Interactions in $\pi_1 \to 3\pi$
item.description: arXiv:2607.14300v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the $\pi_1(1600)$ signal channel of $3\pi$ in the $J^{PC} = 1^{-+} \,[\pi\pi]_{1^{--}}\pi~P$-wave. This channel has recently been analyzed by the COMPASS collaboration using the ``freed-isobar" technique which provides direct experimental access to the lineshape modifications of the $P$-wave $\pi\pi$ sub-channel arising from both final state interactions and production processes such as the Deck mechanism. We motivate a unified formalism combining production effects and final state interactions using the Khuri-Treiman formalism, which is consistent with low-energy unitarity, analyticity, and crossing symmetry, seeded by an initial production amplitude. We demonstrate that the precise lineshape of the $\pi\pi$ mass spectrum can be used to determine the relative strength and complex phase of different production mechanisms contributing to the $3\pi$ final state. We conduct a global fit of the $\pi_1$ freed-isobar data set, yielding a multi-dimensional parameterization of the $\pi_1\to3\pi$ decay amplitude at COMPASS as a function of both decay and production variables. We identify the contributions from short-range production and the Deck mechanism and extract the total $3\pi$ invariant mass dependence which will be important for a future extraction of the $\pi_1$ pole position in the $\rho\pi$ channel.
item.dc:creator: D. Winney, S. Gonz\`alez-Sol\'is, M. Mikhasenko, {\L}. Bibrzycki, C. Fern\'andez-Ram\'irez, V. Mathieu, G. Monta\~na, A. Pilloni, L. Qiu, A. Rodas, A. P. Szczepaniak

item.title: Magnetic field-induced enhancement and quenching of Urca emission in quark matter
item.description: arXiv:2609.00157v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Using first-principles field-theoretic methods, we investigate neutrino emission from strongly magnetized dense quark matter under conditions relevant to compact stars. We account for Landau-level quantization of both electron and quark states and show that it strongly modifies the kinematics of Urca processes. In particular, quark quantization restricts the available phase space in which both quark and electron energies can simultaneously lie near their respective Fermi surfaces. At moderately strong magnetic fields, before pronounced quark quantization sets in, the emission rate tends to increase on average with increasing field strength. In the regime of very strong fields, however, the increasingly restricted phase space first gives rise to Shubnikov--de Haas-type oscillations and then to resonance-like spikes near a discrete sequence of Urca-resonant magnetic field values, separated by regions of strong suppression. Finally, the emission rate becomes nearly completely quenched once $|eB| \gtrsim 6\mu_{e}\mu_{u}$, corresponding to approximately $B\gtrsim 1.5\times 10^{19}~\mbox{G}$ for the representative set of model parameters considered. We also find significant anisotropy in the longitudinal momentum emission near the Urca-resonant magnetic field values.
item.dc:creator: William Gyory, Igor A. Shovkovy

item.title: Stable and causal frames for BDNK hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.28984v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish the existence of families of linearly stable and causal Bemfica-Disconzi-Noronha-Kovtun (BDNK) frames for arbitrary equation of state and set of physical transport coefficients. By developing a method based on simplification of Routh-Hurwitz criteria and telegrapher factorisation of polynomials, we provide six concrete examples of such families, three of which admit conformal limits, for both neutral and charged fluids. These frames have adjustable characteristic speeds and can serve as a starting point for numerical implementations of relativistic hydrodynamics in various settings. In the process we uncover a map between stable and causal frames in neutral fluids and stable and causal frames in charged fluids. We also develop an AI research protocol that can be used to search for such frames in any hydrodynamic theory.
item.dc:creator: Jay Armas

item.title: Negative-Power Density of States in Chiral-Orthogonal Disordered Systems and the IR Phase of QCD
item.description: arXiv:2610.35524v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The recently discovered IR phase of QCD is characterized by an infrared (IR) sector of Dirac modes that separates and dynamically decouples from the bulk of the spectrum, becoming scale invariant in the process [1]. Among key features of this IR sector is the negative power-law behavior of Dirac spectral density near zero with power close to $-1$. Here we start investigating to what extent can this behavior be mimicked by chiral Anderson models. In particular, we study 3-D chiral-orthogonal systems with logarithmic off-diagonal disorder where negative-power ``spikes'' have been observed [2]. We find that for disorders of moderate strength $W$, these models in fact do not have a power-singular density of states (DOS) at zero energy in the thermodynamic limit. Rather, the corresponding power vanishes but the spectrum features a very accurate negative-power behavior on an interval around $E=1$, spreading increasingly closer to $E=0$ and $E=\infty$ with increasing $W$. We connect this to the fact that random hoppings $t$ in these quantum systems are drawn from a scale-invariant $1/t$ distribution regularized via $t \in [e^{-W/2}, e^{W/2}]$, and DOS with negative power can naturally arise inside that range. In fact, we find that power $p$ in the vicinity of energy $E$ satisfies $\lim_{W \to \infty} p(W, E) = -1$ for all $E$ we access. This indicates that, upon removing the cutoff $W$, quantum mechanics transforms the scale-invariant $1/t$ noise into a scale-invariant $1/E$ distribution of eigenstates, which mimics the interpretation of scale-invariant Dirac spectral densities in the IR phase as being due to scale-invariant glue backgrounds [1]. Our results imply that, when modeling the IR phase, the IR cutoff in chiral Anderson systems needs to be tied to their randomness strength $W$ rather than to their lattice size $L$.

item.title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
item.description: arXiv:2610.41082v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the equilibrium structure and stability against radial oscillations of a variety of two-fluid compact objects containing ordinary baryonic matter admixed with cold dark matter coupled through the background spacetime. For the ordinary fluid, we employ a QCD equation of state compatible with chiral effective field theory at nuclear densities (supplemented by the BPS and Negele-Vautherin models at extremely low densities) and with perturbative QCD in the high-density regime while also satisfying also current astrophysical data. For the dark fluid, we assume self-interacting fermionic matter with particle masses of $m_f=$ 2, 5, 10, and 100 GeV and two self-interaction strengths of $y=0.1$ and $10^3$. By scanning a large range of central pressures for both fluids, we identify the presence of dark compact planets, dark white dwarfs, dark neutron stars and the so-called dark oysters. Importantly, these objects are not only in two-fluid hydrostatic equilibrium, but they are also stable against two-fluid radial oscillations. We find that the relative representation of each class in the radially stable sample is strongly sensitive to the combinations of $m_f$ and $y$, with some combinations entirely suppressing some of these object classes within the sampled domain while favoring others. In addition to these classes, strong self-repulsion supports stable, dark-matter-dominated branches with compact ordinary-matter cores and extended dark halos, approaching the self-interacting fermion-star limit. Finally, we calculate the gravitational redshift at the ordinary-matter surface, $z_{\rm OM}$, including the contribution of extended dark-matter halos for which we found radially stable configurations with $z_{\rm OM}>2$.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e C. Jim\'enez, Oscar Pastor, Laura Tolos
